input.subject: Shower hose repair – Flat 14, 44 Lantern Quay (Ref R/PM037-1)
input.body:
Dear Eliza,

Re: Flat 14, 44 Lantern Quay, Alderwick, ZZ9 8ZZ – Ref R/PM037-1

The landlord has asked us to arrange replacement of the leaking shower hose. We are now selecting a contractor, who will contact you directly to arrange a visit. We aim to update you within one working day.

In the meantime, please avoid using the shower if water is leaking, and wipe up any water on the floor to prevent slips or damage. If it is an electric shower and water is reaching the unit or any wiring, switch the shower off at its isolator switch and do not use it. If you are able to send photos of the damaged hose and the leak, that would still help the contractor.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning:
The classifier's "emergency" label seems like overcalling here—a leaking hose is containable if the shower isn't used. But if this is an electric shower, a leak near electrical components could pose a real risk, so I should treat it as urgent and advise the tenant not to use the shower until it's checked, even if it's not a full emergency.

Since no contractor is known yet, I'll need a human to select one. My plan is to log the profile fact, send the tenant safe-use guidance, and escalate to a human for contractor selection at normal priority—no landlord response needed right now, though I could add a brief acknowledgment and set a one-day follow-up hold with the agency.

result.summary: The landlord's reply in event 007, "Please get the shower hose replaced.", tells us to arrange the repair. She doesn't need a reply. The records show no contractor I can assign: none on the ticket, none named by the landlord and no past jobs at the property. So I've passed contractor selection to the operations team. I also emailed the tenant to say the repair is being arranged, with safety advice, and set a follow-up for one day's time.

judgement.why_this_decision: In event 003 we asked the landlord whether she would arrange the repair herself or wanted us to do it. Her reply in event 007 asks us to get the hose replaced. That is a clear go-ahead for the agency to arrange it, and the reply classifier agreed (approve 0.94, unconditional 0.82). The normal next step is to assign a contractor, but I can't pick one without making it up: none is on the ticket, the landlord didn't name one and the property has no job history. A person needs to choose one.

alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no contractor on record or named by the landlord. Picking one would mean inventing a name.
Her message was a clear instruction and needs no response (event 006 asked us to check this).

alternatives_considered.option: Treat it as an emergency dispatch, as the intake classifier suggested
alternatives_considered.why_not: A leaking shower hose can be contained by not using the shower. The tenant got containment advice, including what to do if the shower is electric.

alternatives_considered.option: Ask the landlord for a cost cap first
alternatives_considered.why_not: A hose replacement is a small routine job. The team can check the cost with her if the quote turns out high.
